claims.statement: The dashboard backend is an APIRouter with prefix "/dashboard/api" and a router-level mutation-origin dependency; openswe/api/app.py includes it and then invokes mount_dashboard_ui(app).

openswe/dashboard/__init__.py exposes the router lazily via a PEP 562 __getattr__ so that importing a dashboard submodule does not drag in routes.py, FastAPI, and every API/job module; only the webapp that mounts the router pays that import cost.

GitHub login creates signed state containing a hash of a nonce placed in a short-lived HTTP-only state cookie, then redirects to GitHub; the normal callback verifies the state cookie, exchanges the code, enforces the organization gate, persists the token, and issues a signed session cookie, while a desktop handoff returns a PKCE-bound code without setting that browser cookie.

Session cookie flags derive from the API scheme and whether dashboard and API are same-origin: HTTP is non-Secure SameSite=Lax, same-origin HTTPS is Secure SameSite=Lax, and split-origin HTTPS is Secure SameSite=None.

Every dashboard mutation is guarded by the router-level require_same_origin_for_mutations dependency, which passes GET/HEAD/OPTIONS and bearer-token-only requests but rejects cookie-authenticated mutations whose Origin/Referer is not allowed; WebSockets always receive the origin check.
require_session decodes the session cookie or raises 401, and admin-only endpoints additionally check is_admin.
The thread detail endpoint returns metadata-derived summary only and does not perform server-side message conversion because the client obtains the transcript from the LangGraph state endpoint.

The cloud terminal is exposed as POST /threads/{id}/terminal/connect (returning a WebSocket URL, subprotocol, and short-lived signed ticket) plus a WS /threads/{id}/terminal that requires a LangSmith sandbox, is capacity-bounded by a semaphore to 20 concurrent sessions, and bridges the browser to a PTY shell in the thread's sandbox.

The browser calls /dashboard/api/* as a same-origin relative path so the session cookie is sent, and Vite proxies those calls to the Python backend in development rather than sending them cross-origin.

In deployed builds ui/server/backend-proxy.ts is the Nitro handler for /dashboard/api/** and /webhooks/**, reads DASHBOARD_API_URL per request, keeps OAuth 3xx hops with redirect: "manual", and fails if DASHBOARD_API_URL is unset rather than using a production backend default.

During SSR the dashboard fetch layer copies the incoming request's cookie header onto forwarded requests because credentials: "include" is meaningless on the server, and it targets DASHBOARD_API_URL directly instead of a relative origin.

The experimental Electron desktop app ships the compiled web UI at an internal open-swe://app origin and proxies /dashboard/api/* to the user-configured backend so the renderer never sees a LangSmith key or calls the raw LangGraph API; desktop session handoff is exchanged at POST /auth/desktop/exchange with a PKCE verifier.

BackendSupervisor lazily starts a token-authenticated loopback LangGraph server on 127.0.0.1 from langgraph.desktop.json in development or the bundled configuration when packaged; openswe/desktop.py permits a desktop run only for an existing allowlisted local project or a desktop-managed worktree and builds a LocalShellBackend rooted at that project.
Authenticated users may read any thread whose metadata source is surfaced, while unsurfaced threads return 404; posting additionally requires admin for admin threads and automation threads.
Repository-scoped agent-instruction records normalize owner/repo, and non-empty text for a run's resolved repository is appended to the main agent prompt; lookup failures are fail-soft.

Review styles are repository-access-controlled records with an idle/running/completed/failed lifecycle; retrieval reconciles running analyses, concurrent analysis returns 409, and saved prompts allow a terminal or missing analysis run to resolve as completed.

Schedule listing requires authentication, but schedule creation, update, test triggering, and deletion require admin authorization; schedules are workspace-scoped records with cron and separate run state.

Thread discovery is participant/admin scoped: all=true is reserved for administrators; ordinary page and project listings derive candidates from participant metadata, while pinned entries are fetched from a per-login store and independently checked for current readability.

Thread status normalization reports an interrupted latest run as interrupted even while the thread is temporarily busy, and marking a non-running thread viewed is fail-soft if the metadata update fails.

The local-graph proxy removes renderer cookies, injects the supervisor's random bearer token, and exposes the stable /local-graph agent configuration; startup polls that authenticated loopback server, while shutdown escalates from SIGTERM to SIGKILL after its timeout.

For configurable.source == "desktop", the agent factory selects the local backend rather than a cloud sandbox, disables cloud sandbox file downloads, uses local model defaults, exposes state-backed user skills rather than organization skills, and routes scratch artifacts to sanitized per-thread filesystem backends outside the project.

The paginated thread listing applies metadata filters before summary construction, refreshes potentially active latest runs with concurrency limited to eight, and applies viewed/status filters only after summary construction.

The backend dashboard UI mount serves a configured or in-repository static build at the root, gives hashed assets immutable caching and the shell no-cache, declines reserved server paths and non-HTML unknown paths, and can instead reverse-proxy a Vite dev server while keeping the backend origin.
The dashboard UI catch-all must be registered after API routes; keep_dashboard_ui_last moves it behind subsequently registered routes.
At application construction, DASHBOARD_ALLOWED_ORIGINS configures credentialed CORS, but a wildcard origin is rejected because credentials are enabled.

The browser opens a server-sent events stream at GET /dashboard/api/ui-invalidations?t=... with topic names and staleness ages; the invalidation hub manages a single shared PostgreSQL LISTEN connection across replicas, with each replica tracking subscribed Stream topics in memory and delivering push notifications when invalidations commit.

The UI invalidation stream first reports which subscribed topics were invalidated within the staleness window (accounting for PostgreSQL lag), then emits every subsequent invalidation once per frame, so clients refetch only the stale queries while avoiding polling and staying synchronized across network gaps.

A Topic is a fully qualified name (e.g., workspaces, threads/thread-id, review-styles/owner/repo); authorization checks which topic keys a session may hear before allowing the subscription, ensuring that keyed topics do not expose private records.

Review styles hold an approval mode (which delegates approval authority to the analyzer when set) and a repository-held prompt that steers the analyzer behavior; readings return summaries containing findings; concurrent analysis attempts return 409 to prevent redundant work.

PR review findings are retrieved in batches via POST /dashboard/api/reviews/summaries (up to 100 references per call), and include tool-generated issues (code smells, security, etc.) surfaced alongside the human review conversation; review_conversation router manages the async chat interface for proposing comments and sharing insights.

The dashboard displays agent runs using the LangGraph v3 protocol stream, receiving state snapshots and intermediate event frames from /threads/{id}/stream; events include tool invocations with schemas and outputs, state updates, and checkpoint markers for real-time progress display.

Subagent visibility in the UI is determined by tool events in the run manifest; tool events carrying subagent thread IDs are rendered as clickable references, allowing users to navigate into nested invocations; tool events also provide schema, input parameters, and parsed output for domain-specific UI visualizations.

On desktop runs, the UI avoids exposing tool results containing credentials or artifacts; instead it renders locally-scoped results from the supervised backend that are safe to display in the browser, preventing credential leakage while preserving the LangGraph protocol.
